key_insight: HVAF-sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr delivered the lowest measured wear rate and best corrosion resistance, while HVOF achieved the highest hardness.
engineering_relevance: The results support HVAF as a promising coating process for 304 stainless steel components exposed to combined wear and corrosion.
method: Deposited WC-10Co-4Cr on 304 stainless steel using APS, detonation spraying, HVOF, and HVAF.
Compared microstructure, Vickers hardness, friction, and volumetric wear rates.
Evaluated corrosion performance using electrochemical measurements.
evidence_signal: HVAF showed a wear rate of (1.10±0.01)×10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m), versus (36.82±0.80)×10⁻⁵ for bare steel, and the lowest coating corrosion current density at 1.75±0.02 µA/cm².
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions or corrosion medium, limiting direct transfer of the rankings to service environments.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
